questions.question: What effect does increasing the temperature parameter have on text generation?
choices: It makes the output more deterministic and repetitive
It flattens the probability distribution, making lower-probability tokens more likely and increasing output diversity
It increases the number of tokens generated
It makes the model only choose the highest-probability token
questions.explanation: Temperature scales the logits before softmax. Higher temperature (e.g., 1.5+) flattens the distribution, making rare tokens more likely. Lower temperature (e.g., 0.2) sharpens it toward the top token, making output more focused.

questions.question: How does top-k sampling differ from top-p (nucleus) sampling?
choices: Top-k selects the k most probable tokens; top-p selects the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds p
Top-k and top-p are identical algorithms with different names
Top-k filters by token length; top-p filters by probability
questions.explanation: Top-k always considers exactly k tokens regardless of probability spread. Top-p is adaptive — it includes as many tokens as needed to reach probability mass p, so the candidate set size varies depending on how confident the model is.

questions.question: When would you use temperature = 0 (greedy decoding) in production?
choices: When you want the most creative and diverse outputs
When you need deterministic, reproducible outputs for tasks like code generation, classification, or factual Q&A
When training the model for the first time
When you want to explore the full vocabulary distribution
questions.explanation: Temperature 0 always picks the highest-probability token, making output fully deterministic. This is ideal for production tasks requiring consistency and reproducibility, like extracting structured data or generating code.
